extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO, OED staff, and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria used by the USPTO Director and OED to impose reciprocal discipline, probation, reinstatement, and related notices when a practitioner is disciplined by another jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, when a practitioner subject to the disciplinary jurisdiction of the Office is disciplined by another jurisdiction, the USPTO Director is required to impose reciprocal discipline that is identical to the discipline imposed by the other jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to imposing reciprocal discipline, the USPTO Director provides an opportunity for the practitioner to show that reciprocal discipline should not be imposed for one of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d). If the practitioner offers no objection or no showing that meets the § 11.24(d) standard, reciprocal suspension is appropriate (here, respondent consented and offered no objection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Available defenses to reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may avoid imposition of identical reciprocal discipline by establishing one of the statutory/regulated reasons listed in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) (i.e., that the imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted for one of the specified reasons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order gives the respondent forty days to file a response containing all information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the other jurisdiction would be unwarranted under § 11.24(d)(1). In this case the respondent offered no such showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure and timing under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, a suspended practitioner cannot resume practicing before the Office until she has been reinstated by the OED Director or the USPTO Director and must file a petition for reinstatement that meets the requirements of § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order permitted the respondent to seek reinstatement after serving twenty-four months of a three-year suspension. Any petition must meet the requirements of § 11.60; mere reinstatement in a State bar does not automatically reinstate practice before the USPTO absent compliance with § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary suspension or waiver of non-statutory requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.3, in an extraordinary situation when justice requires, any requirement of this Part which is not a requirement of statute may be suspended or waived by the USPTO Director or designee on petition by any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension/waiver is reserved for extraordinary circumstances where justice requires; routine or unsupported requests for suspension of § 11.60 requirements will be denied (respondent provided no basis for suspension and the Office found her situation not extraordinary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for discipline: ethical violations (state court findings invoked)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline may be predicated on the respondent's violations as determined by a duly constituted state authority (e.g., failing to maintain client trust balance; misappropriating client funds; gross negligence in managing client trust account; failing to promptly pay client funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order relied on the California Supreme Court's findings that respondent willfully misappropriated $13,604.67, committed an act of moral turpitude due to gross negligence managing the client trust account, and failed to promptly pay client funds — violations of California Rule of Professional Conduct 4-100(A) and (B)(4) and Business and Professions Code § 6106 — and treated those findings as the basis for reciprocal discipline under the USPTO regulation cited (including 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation terms and conditions; consequences for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may place a respondent on probation for a specified period (here, three years) and may condition reinstatement and continued practice on satisfying other provisions (e.g., § 11.14(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, during probation, the OED Director believes the respondent failed to comply with the Final Order or any Disciplinary Rule, the OED Director may issue an Order to Show Cause, send it where the respondent receives mail, grant fifteen days to respond, and, if still unsatisfied, deliver the record to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to an additional one year. These are the procedural steps and potential consequences for probationary noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's authority in enforcement and reinstatement considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may consider a respondent's purported failure to comply with the Final Order or Disciplinary Rules in connection with any reinstatement request and may pursue further discipline under the provisions of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.34 through 11.57.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even while a respondent remains not yet reinstated, alleged violations can be considered in deciding reinstatement petitions or may prompt separate disciplinary proceedings; the OED Director has discretion to act on compliance concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause process and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion the respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director may issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to where respondent reasonably receives mail, and grant fifteen days to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the 15-day response period and consideration of any reply, the OED Director may forward the Order to Show Cause, respondent's response, and supporting argument/evidence to the USPTO Director and request immediate additional suspension for up to one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette providing details of the suspension and probation, the basis for discipline, reinstatement conditions, and explicit statements about the practitioner's authorization (e.g., not authorized to practice patent law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Notice included in the Final Order describes the practitioner's suspension, basis (including state court citation and rule violations), the earliest date to seek reinstatement, probation terms, and the practitioner's lack of authorization to practice patent law before the USPTO; disciplinary decisions are also posted in the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to appropriate offices and state authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct the OED Director to give notice of the final decision to appropriate employees of the Office and to interested departments, agencies, courts of the United States, and to appropriate authorities of any State in which the practitioner is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures other government entities and state bars receive formal notification of the USPTO disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of consent or failure to object in reciprocal discipline proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a respondent expressly consents to reciprocal discipline or states an understanding that reciprocal discipline is automatic and offers no argument under § 11.24(d), the Director will determine reciprocal suspension is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The respondent's January 3, 2012 response expressly acknowledged that 'reciprocal suspension with the US PTO is automatic' and offered no objections; the Office relied on that lack of objection in granting reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on practice areas (patent vs. trademark/non-patent matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order should state whether the respondent is authorized to practice patent law before the US PTO; a practitioner not registered to practice patent law remains unauthorized to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice explicitly informs the public that the respondent is not authorized to practice patent law before the USPTO, clarifying scope of permitted practice (trademark and other non-patent matters only, subject to suspension/reinstatement provisions).
